processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea, so processing depends on the maker and the target style. No single method belongs to it.
harvest_season: Not well documented in the terms of a single picking; as with green teas in general, spring buds and young leaves are the prized lots.
appearance_dry: Depends on the style made from it; as a green tea, expect the look of an ordinary spring green.
appearance_liquor: As with most Chinese greens, pale yellow-green and clear.
appearance_wet: As with most Chinese greens, soft green buds and leaves.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for the cultivar alone; the cup depends on what the leaf has been made into.

brewing.notes: General advice for a Chinese green; brew to the style of the actual tea.

vintage_note: Seldom sold to drinkers under this name. Green tea from any cultivar is usually sold as the current year's spring harvest and is best drunk within a year; a tea made in another style follows the habits of that style.
description:
Fuyun 6 is a named Chinese tea cultivar. Drinkers rarely meet the name on a label, because it describes the plant and not a finished tea.

It shows up mostly in plant science. Fujian researchers have used it as the male parent in a cross with Baijiguan, the yellow-leaved Wuyi bush, to build a genetic map, and it has been compared with Meizhan for resistance to a tea mite.

Because the cultivar is not itself a style, there is no fixed taste to promise. Treat any tea made from it according to its style, and brew it as a green if that is what it was made into.

If a seller names it, ask what was made from the leaf, where and when. That tells you more about the cup than the cultivar name does.
history: The name appears in the work of Chinese tea researchers, including a 2024 genetic mapping paper from the Fujian Academy of Agricultural Sciences' tea institute, which used it as a parent. Its own breeding record is little documented in general references.
